properties.text: The fork trigger function MUST only execute state upgrade when slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH == 0 (epoch boundary). For all slots where slot % SLOTS_PER_EPOCH != 0, the state MUST remain unchanged.

The fork trigger MUST fire exactly once at FULU_FORK_EPOCH. For all epochs E != FULU_FORK_EPOCH, the fork trigger MUST NOT invoke upgrade_to_fulu. For epoch E == FULU_FORK_EPOCH at an epoch boundary slot, the fork trigger MUST invoke upgrade_to_fulu exactly once.

Once the Fulu fork has been triggered, the state upgrade is irreversible. For all subsequent slots S > FULU_FORK_EPOCH * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH, state.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. There exists no valid state transition that reverts fork.current_version to a pre-Fulu version.

For all fields F in electra.BeaconState where F is not in {fork, proposer_lookahead}, upgrade_to_fulu(pre).F == pre.F. The upgrade function MUST preserve all existing state fields except fork and proposer_lookahead.
After upgrade_to_fulu(pre), the resulting state MUST satisfy: post.fork.previous_version == pre.fork.current_version. The fork version chain MUST be maintained without gaps.
After upgrade_to_fulu(pre), the resulting state MUST satisfy: post.fork.current_version == FULU_FORK_VERSION. The fork version MUST be set to the exact Fulu fork version constant.
After upgrade_to_fulu(pre), post.fork.epoch == get_current_epoch(pre). The fork epoch recorded in the state MUST match the epoch at which the upgrade was triggered.

After upgrade_to_fulu(pre), post.proposer_lookahead == initialize_proposer_lookahead(pre). The proposer_lookahead field MUST be freshly initialized from the pre-state and MUST NOT be copied from any pre-state field.
upgrade_to_fulu MUST be a pure function: for all pre-states S, calling upgrade_to_fulu(S) MUST NOT modify S. The pre-state MUST be identical before and after the call.

Fork epoch constants MUST be strictly ordered: GENESIS_EPOCH < ALTAIR_FORK_EPOCH < BELLATRIX_FORK_EPOCH < CAPELLA_FORK_EPOCH < DENEB_FORK_EPOCH < ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH < FULU_FORK_EPOCH. No two fork epoch constants may be equal.

For any valid epoch value E, compute_fork_version(E) MUST take exactly one branch and return exactly one fork version. The function MUST be total and deterministic: for all E >= 0, exactly one of the conditional branches is taken.
compute_fork_version MUST always return a valid Version type. The function MUST NOT raise exceptions, return null, or return an invalid version for any non-negative epoch input.
For all data column sidecars, sidecar.index MUST be in the range [0, NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS). verify_data_column_sidecar MUST return False for any sidecar with index >= NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS.
verify_data_column_sidecar MUST return False when len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) == 0. A data column sidecar with no KZG commitments is always invalid.

For all valid data column sidecars at epoch E, len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) <= get_blob_parameters(E).max_blobs_per_block. verify_data_column_sidecar MUST return False when the commitment count exceeds the epoch-dependent maximum.

For all valid data column sidecars, len(sidecar.column) == len(sidecar.kzg_commitments) == len(sidecar.kzg_proofs). verify_data_column_sidecar MUST return False if any of these three array lengths differ.

In verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs, all cells in a single column MUST share the same cell index, which equals the column index. The cell_indices array MUST be [CellIndex(sidecar.index)] repeated len(sidecar.column) times.

verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch MUST receive arrays of consistent length: len(commitments_bytes) == len(cell_indices) == len(cells) == len(proofs_bytes). Calls with inconsistent array lengths MUST be rejected.
KZG_COMMITMENTS_INCLUSION_PROOF_DEPTH MUST equal 4. The Merkle inclusion proof linking kzg_commitments to the block body_root MUST use exactly this depth.

verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof MUST verify that hash_tree_root(sidecar.kzg_commitments) is a valid Merkle leaf at the correct generalized index within the BeaconBlockBody tree rooted at body_root. A tampered kzg_commitments set MUST cause the inclusion proof to fail.
DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT MUST equal 128. This constant MUST be identical across all client implementations.

For all valid column indices C, compute_subnet_for_data_column_sidecar(C) MUST return a SubnetID in the range [0, DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT). The result is computed as C % DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT.

In the gossip validation pipeline (SG-006), a data column sidecar MUST NOT be forwarded to peers until ALL REJECT checks have been passed. The pipeline MUST execute checks sequentially: structural validation, subnet validation, slot timing, proposer signature, parent validation, ancestry, inclusion proof, KZG proofs, deduplication, and proposer schedule.

When a gossip validation check results in IGNORE, the sidecar MUST NOT be forwarded but MUST be eligible for re-processing at a later time (queuing). IGNORE is distinct from REJECT in that IGNORE does not permanently discard the message.

For each data column sidecar processed by the gossip validation pipeline, exactly one path from q_init to q_final MUST be taken. The pipeline MUST be deterministic: the same sidecar and state MUST always produce the same outcome (ACCEPT, REJECT, or IGNORE).

The deduplication key for data column sidecars MUST be the tuple (slot, proposer_index, sidecar.index). Only the first valid sidecar for each unique key MUST be accepted; all subsequent sidecars with the same key MUST be IGNORED.

When the proposer shuffling computation is not yet available for a given slot, proposer verification MUST result in IGNORE rather than REJECT. The sidecar MUST NOT be permanently discarded due to deferred shuffling computation.

max_blobs_per_block MUST be epoch-dependent via get_blob_parameters. For all epochs E, get_blob_parameters(E).max_blobs_per_block returns the correct maximum for that epoch, and len(block.body.blob_kzg_commitments) <= get_blob_parameters(E).max_blobs_per_block for all valid blocks at epoch E.

Blocks with zero blob KZG commitments (len(blob_kzg_commitments) == 0) MUST be considered valid with respect to the blob commitment count check. There is no lower bound on the number of blob commitments.
A DataColumnSidecarsByRange response MUST contain no more than count * NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS sidecars total.
A DataColumnSidecarsByRange response MUST contain no more than MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS sidecars regardless of the request parameters.

Sidecars in a DataColumnSidecarsByRange response MUST be ordered by (slot, column_index). For all consecutive pairs (s_i, s_{i+1}) in the response, either s_i.slot < s_{i+1}.slot, or (s_i.slot == s_{i+1}.slot AND s_i.column_index < s_{i+1}.column_index).

If any sidecar for a given block is included in a DataColumnSidecarsByRange response, ALL sidecars of that block that match the requested columns MUST be included. Partial block responses are not permitted.
All sidecars in a DataColumnSidecarsByRange response MUST be from the current fork choice chain. Sidecars from orphaned or non-canonical blocks MUST NOT be included.

data_column_serve_range MUST equal [max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH), current_epoch]. Requests outside this range MUST receive a ResourceUnavailable(3) response.

For DataColumnSidecarsByRoot requests, the total requested_columns_count (sum of len(r.columns) for all identifiers) MUST NOT exceed MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS. Requests exceeding this limit MUST be rejected.

For DataColumnSidecarsByRoot, minimum_request_epoch MUST equal max(current_epoch - MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, FULU_FORK_EPOCH). Blocks with epoch < minimum_request_epoch MUST be skipped.

If a node has a sidecar that matches a DataColumnSidecarsByRoot request and the block passes all validation requirements, the node MUST include at least one sidecar in the response. Nodes MUST NOT withhold available sidecars for valid requests.
Sidecars served via DataColumnSidecarsByRoot MUST only come from blocks that pass gossip validation. Sidecars from blocks that fail gossip validation MUST NOT be served.
Sidecars MUST NOT be served via DataColumnSidecarsByRoot for blocks that fail the beacon-chain state transition function. Failed state transitions indicate an invalid block.

During distributed blob publishing (SG-010), blobs retrieved from the local execution layer via engine_getBlobsV2 MUST skip cryptographic verification. The local EL is unconditionally trusted for blob data integrity.

During distributed blob publishing, data column sidecars MUST only be published on gossip subnets to which the local node is subscribed (either via custody duties or sampling duties). Publishing on non-subscribed subnets MUST NOT occur.

The anti-equivocation cache MUST be updated during distributed blob publishing regardless of whether the sidecar is actually published to any gossip subnet. Cache update MUST occur even when the node is not subscribed to the relevant subnet.

Imported data columns from distributed blob publishing MUST behave identically to data columns received via gossip. They MUST be stored, served to requesters, and tracked by the anti-equivocation cache in the same manner.

The BlobSidecarsByRange endpoint MUST be fully deprecated and respond with empty lists after current_epoch >= FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS. No blob sidecars MUST be served after this epoch.
During the Fulu transition period, BlobSidecarsByRange MUST only serve blob sidecars from pre-Fulu epochs. Blob sidecars at or after FULU_FORK_EPOCH MUST NOT be served via this endpoint.
Peers MUST NOT be penalized (peer score reduction) for requesting blob sidecars from FULU_FORK_EPOCH during the transition period. Transition-boundary requests are legitimate and expected.
The ENR eth2 field value MUST always be exactly 16 bytes (SSZ-encoded ENRForkID). For all node states and fork configurations, the encoded ENRForkID MUST produce exactly 16 bytes.
For BPO (Blob Parameter Only) forks, the ENR encoding MUST NOT change next_fork_version; it MUST remain equal to current_fork_version. Only next_fork_epoch MUST be set to the planned BPO fork epoch.
When no future fork is planned, the ENR encoding MUST set next_fork_version = current_fork_version AND next_fork_epoch = FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH.

The epoch used for ENR eth2 field computation MUST be determined by wall-clock time, not by the node's sync state. An unsynced node MUST still advertise the correct fork digest based on current wall-clock epoch.

The BlobSidecarsByRoot endpoint MUST be fully deprecated after FULU_FORK_EPOCH + MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_BLOB_SIDECARS_REQUESTS, returning empty responses. During the transition period, it MUST only serve pre-Fulu blob sidecars.

The p256verify precompile at address 0x100 MUST NOT revert under any circumstances except out-of-gas. For all possible calldata inputs, the precompile MUST return either empty bytes (invalid) or the 32-byte success value 0x01 (valid).

The p256verify precompile MUST perform input validation checks in a specific sequential order: (1) input length == 160 bytes, (2) 0 < r < n, (3) 0 < s < n, (4) 0 <= qx < p, (5) 0 <= qy < p, (6) (qx, qy) is on the secp256r1 curve, (7) (qx, qy) is not the point at infinity. Any check failure at step i MUST return empty bytes without proceeding to step i+1.

The p256verify precompile MUST perform a mandatory point-at-infinity check on R' during signature verification. If R' is the point at infinity, the verification MUST fail (return empty bytes). This fixes the RIP-7212 vulnerability.

The p256verify precompile MUST use modular comparison r' == r (mod n) rather than direct equality r' == r for the final signature check. This fixes the RIP-7212 vulnerability for edge-case x-coordinates exceeding the subgroup order n.

The p256verify precompile MUST charge exactly 6900 gas for every invocation regardless of the execution path taken (early validation failure or full signature verification). The gas cost MUST be fixed and not depend on input values.

For all valid transaction types, gasLimit MUST NOT exceed GAS_CAP (16777216 = 2^24). Transactions with gasLimit > 16777216 MUST be rejected at both the transaction pool layer and the block validation layer.

The gas cap MUST be enforced at exactly two independent layers: (1) transaction pool admission (SG-001) and (2) block validation (SG-002). A bypass at layer 1 MUST be caught by layer 2. Both layers MUST use the identical constant GAS_CAP = 16777216.

Block validation MUST iterate over ALL transactions in the block before acceptance. A single transaction with gasLimit > 16777216 MUST invalidate the entire block. There MUST be no early-exit optimization that could skip checking some transactions.

The gas cap MUST apply uniformly to all transaction types (legacy, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844 blob transactions) regardless of the block gas limit. The gas cap is independent of and may be less than the block gas limit.

The ModExp precompile gas cost function multiplication_complexity MUST have a minimum output of 16 for all inputs. For all (base_length, modulus_length) pairs, multiplication_complexity(max(base_length, modulus_length)) >= 16.
For ModExp inputs where max(base_length, modulus_length) <= 32, multiplication_complexity MUST be exactly 16. The word-based formula MUST only apply for operands larger than 32 bytes.
The ModExp iteration_count MUST always be >= 1 for all non-trivial inputs. The max(iteration_count, 1) clamp for large exponents MUST ensure no zero-cost execution paths exist.

The ModExp large exponent multiplier MUST be 16 (doubled from EIP-2565's value of 8). For all inputs with exponent_length > 32, the iteration_count MUST use the multiplier 16 for the exponent head processing.
The ModExp minimum gas floor MUST be 500. The final gas cost MUST be computed as max(500, floor(multiplication_complexity * iteration_count)) with NO division by 3.

The ModExp gas cost formula MUST be deterministic: for identical input parameters (base_length, modulus_length, exponent_length, and data), all client implementations MUST compute the identical gas cost value using only integer arithmetic.

The secp256r1 curve parameters (field modulus p, subgroup order n, base point G, cofactor 1) MUST be exactly as defined in NIST SP 800-186. All client implementations MUST use identical curve parameters.

For all callers of the p256verify precompile, a return of empty bytes (0 bytes) MUST be interpreted as signature verification failure, and a return of exactly 32 bytes with value 0x01 MUST be interpreted as signature verification success. No other return values are valid.

BLOB_SCHEDULE entries MUST have unique and monotonically meaningful epoch values, all >= FULU_FORK_EPOCH. Duplicate epoch entries or entries with epoch < FULU_FORK_EPOCH MUST NOT exist in any valid BLOB_SCHEDULE configuration.
All execution clients MUST implement identical BLOB_SCHEDULE configurations. For all epochs E and all compliant client implementations C1, C2: get_blob_parameters_C1(E) == get_blob_parameters_C2(E).

The proposer_lookahead MUST shift correctly at epoch boundaries, maintaining exactly (MIN_SEED_LOOKAHEAD + 1) * SLOTS_PER_EPOCH entries. The shift operation MUST NOT have off-by-one errors in the epoch computation.

The fork digest XOR with hash(epoch + max_blobs_per_block) MUST produce different fork digests for different blob parameter configurations. Nodes with incompatible blob parameters MUST be segregated on the gossip network.

The epoch processing pipeline MUST execute its 15 sequential sub-processes in strict order. State mutations from earlier steps MUST be visible to later steps. Reordering any two sub-processes MUST be treated as a consensus-breaking change.

Proposer indices MUST be deterministically derived from the seed, active validator set, and slot. For all honest validators V1, V2 with identical beacon state S: compute_proposer(S, slot) on V1 == compute_proposer(S, slot) on V2.

The KZG trusted setup (KZG_SETUP_G1_MONOMIAL, KZG_SETUP_G2_MONOMIAL) is assumed to have been honestly generated with all toxic waste destroyed. This is the foundational cryptographic assumption: if compromised, an adversary can forge KZG proofs for arbitrary polynomials.

The hash function hash_to_bls_field used in Fiat-Shamir challenge computation MUST behave as a random oracle. The domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN MUST be globally unique. All verifier-relevant data (commitments, cell indices, cells, proofs) MUST be included in the hash input.

bytes_to_bls_field and bls_field_to_bytes MUST be correct inverse operations for all valid field elements. For all valid field elements f: bytes_to_bls_field(bls_field_to_bytes(f)) == f. Serialization MUST be injective.

Data recovery (recover_polynomialcoeff, recover_cells_and_kzg_proofs) MUST require at least 50% of cells (CELLS_PER_EXT_BLOB / 2) to be available. Attempts to recover with fewer cells MUST fail or raise an error.
Validators MUST retain data column sidecars for at least MIN_EPOCHS_FOR_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS_REQUESTS epochs. During this retention period, validators MUST serve sidecars when requested by peers.

divide_polynomialcoeff MUST only be called with a non-zero divisor polynomial. The leading coefficient of the divisor MUST be nonzero. Calls violating this pre-condition MUST NOT occur in any valid protocol execution path.
interpolate_polynomialcoeff MUST only be called with distinct x-values. For all pairs (i, j) where i != j: xs[i] != xs[j]. Duplicate x-values would cause division by zero in the finite field.

The bilinear pairing check e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl MUST be sound: it MUST reject with overwhelming probability (negligible soundness error) when the underlying KZG polynomial commitment relationship does not hold.

The deposit contract address MUST be exactly DEPOSIT_CONTRACT_ADDRESS (0x00000000219ab540356cbb839cbe05303d7705fa). The DEPOSIT_EVENT_SIGNATURE_HASH MUST be exactly 0x649bbc62d0e31342afea4e5cd82d4049e7e1ee912fc0889aa790803be39038c5. Only logs matching BOTH the address AND the event signature MUST be processed as deposits.

extract_deposit_data MUST validate that deposit event data is exactly 576 bytes with fixed offsets: PUBKEY_OFFSET=160, WC_OFFSET=256, AMOUNT_OFFSET=320, SIGNATURE_OFFSET=384, INDEX_OFFSET=512. Any deviation from these exact values MUST trigger InvalidBlock.

Receipt processing order (block_output.receipt_keys) MUST deterministically define deposit request ordering. For all compliant execution clients processing the same block, the resulting deposit_requests byte array MUST be identical.

trie_get MUST return a valid (non-None) receipt for every key in block_output.receipt_keys. A None return MUST trigger an assertion failure that halts execution rather than silently skipping deposits.

RLP encoding of accounts MUST be deterministic and canonical. The tuple ordering (nonce, balance, storage_root, code_hash) in encode_account MUST be strictly maintained across all implementations for consensus compatibility.

EIP-7702 Authorization tuples MUST be validated for: (1) chain_id matching the current chain, (2) nonce matching the authorizer's current nonce, (3) valid ECDSA signature (y_parity, r, s) recovering to the expected authorizer address. All three checks MUST pass before the authorization is accepted.

compute_requests_hash MUST use a two-level SHA-256 construction: each request is individually hashed, then all request digests are fed into an outer SHA-256 hash. The order of requests MUST be preserved. Any reordering MUST produce a different hash.

A forged BLS signature on a signed_block_header in a data column sidecar MUST be detected and the sidecar MUST be REJECTED during gossip validation at the proposer signature check step. BLS signature verification MUST occur before proposer schedule verification.

Gossip validation checks MUST be ordered from cheapest to most expensive: structural checks first, then subnet validation (modulo), then slot timing, then signature verification, then parent/fork checks, and finally KZG/Merkle proofs last. Early rejection at cheap steps MUST avoid expensive cryptographic operations.

Data column sidecar integrity MUST be verified through three independent layers: (1) structural validation via verify_data_column_sidecar (index bounds, non-empty commitments, max blobs, equal lengths), (2) KZG proof verification via verify_data_column_sidecar_kzg_proofs (cryptographic cell-commitment binding), (3) Merkle inclusion proof via verify_data_column_sidecar_inclusion_proof (kzg_commitments bound to block body_root). All three layers MUST pass for acceptance.

Both DataColumnSidecarsByRange and DataColumnSidecarsByRoot endpoints MUST enforce MAX_REQUEST_DATA_COLUMN_SIDECARS as an absolute upper bound on response size. Requests that would exceed this bound MUST be truncated or rejected.

If engine_getBlobsV2 fails, times out, or returns incomplete blob data during distributed blob publishing, the publishing process MUST abort gracefully without crashing the node. The anti-equivocation cache MUST NOT be polluted by a failed publishing attempt.

A non-proposer node attempting to inject a sidecar claiming to be from a legitimate proposer MUST be rejected by the gossip validation pipeline. The proposer_index check (q_check_expected_proposer) MUST verify the sidecar's proposer against the expected proposer for the slot derived from beacon state shuffling.

A compromised local execution layer returning tampered blob data via engine_getBlobsV2 MUST NOT be detectable by the local consensus layer (since EL blobs skip verification). However, other network participants verifying the published data columns via KZG proof verification MUST reject invalid columns. This is a known trust assumption that MUST be documented.

During BPO fork transitions, the ENR eth2 encoding MUST correctly distinguish between three cases: (1) no future fork: next_fork_version = current, next_fork_epoch = FAR_FUTURE_EPOCH; (2) regular fork: next_fork_version = planned version, next_fork_epoch = planned epoch; (3) BPO fork: next_fork_version = current (unchanged), next_fork_epoch = planned epoch. Incorrect classification MUST cause peering incompatibility.

If fork epoch constants (FULU_FORK_EPOCH, ELECTRA_FORK_EPOCH, etc.) are tampered with or diverge between client implementations, the node MUST compute incorrect fork versions (P2P SG-001), fork at the wrong time (fork SG-001), or produce incorrect fork upgrades (fork SG-002), resulting in a consensus-detectable chain split.

The recursive FFT implementation MUST only accept inputs whose length is a power of 2. len(vals) MUST equal len(roots_of_unity). All protocol-defined constants (FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_EXT_BLOB, FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL) MUST be powers of 2.

bit_reversal_permutation MUST be applied consistently across all encoding and decoding paths: polynomial_eval_to_coeff (SG-007), coset_shift_for_cell (SG-016), coset_for_cell (SG-017), and recover_polynomialcoeff (SG-023). An inconsistency in any path MUST produce misaligned evaluations leading to verification failure.

After polynomial recovery (recover_polynomialcoeff), the recovered polynomial MUST be truncated to degree < FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB (the first FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB coefficients). High-degree coefficients (beyond FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB) MUST be verified to be zero to confirm correct recovery.

After data recovery, the regenerated cells and proofs MUST be verified against the original KZG commitment using verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch. This post-recovery verification step MUST detect inconsistent input cells that lead to recovery of an incorrect polynomial.

Custody requirement for each validator MUST be deterministically computed as: clamp(total_node_balance // BALANCE_PER_ADDITIONAL_CUSTODY_GROUP, VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT, NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS). The minimum MUST be VALIDATOR_CUSTODY_REQUIREMENT and the maximum MUST be NUMBER_OF_CUSTODY_GROUPS.

In private transaction submission channels (e.g., Flashbots, MEV-Boost relays), block-level validation (SG-002 of EIP-7825) MUST serve as the ultimate enforcement point for the gas cap regardless of how transactions enter the block. Bypassing the txpool layer MUST NOT compromise the gas cap guarantee.

Client implementations MUST use sufficiently large integer types (256-bit or arbitrary precision) for ModExp gas calculations. The computation 2 * words^2 and complexity * iterations MUST NOT overflow. Implicit bounds from calldata size, block gas limit, and EIP-7825 transaction gas cap MUST limit the maximum computable values.

The coset FFT evaluation domain (using PRIMITIVE_ROOT_OF_UNITY as shift_factor) MUST be chosen such that the vanishing polynomial is nonzero at all evaluation points. This algebraic guarantee MUST prevent division-by-zero during the recovery division step.

The Fiat-Shamir challenge computation MUST include the domain separator, all commitment indices, all cell indices, all coset evaluations, and all proofs in a deterministic and canonical order. Omitting or reordering any component MUST change the resulting challenge r, preventing selective forgery.

Wall-clock time MUST be reasonably synchronized across nodes. Slot timing checks in gossip validation (future slot IGNORE, finalized slot IGNORE) depend on current_slot accuracy. Clock skew beyond acceptable bounds MUST be detected and flagged.

NUMBER_OF_COLUMNS and DATA_COLUMN_SIDECAR_SUBNET_COUNT MUST be network-wide constants identical across all nodes. Disagreement on these values between any two honest nodes MUST fragment the gossip network and MUST be treated as a critical misconfiguration.

The finalized checkpoint used in gossip validation and RPC range computation MUST reflect supermajority agreement. The finalized checkpoint MUST also be an ancestor of any accepted block during gossip validation (q_check_finalized_ancestor).

The gossip validation pipeline MUST use IGNORE (rather than REJECT) for conditions that depend on local node state: parent not seen, future slot, pre-finalized slot, and duplicate sidecar. This MUST prevent peers from definitively inferring local node state from rejection messages.
